title: Deep learning reveals migrating foreshocks during laboratory fault nucleation
summary: In biaxial stick-slip experiments on a 0.85 m saw-cut granodiorite fault, the AEbagging ensemble deep-learning picker generated acoustic-emission catalogs for eight laboratory earthquake cycles. The model-derived catalogs revealed a foreshock sequence migrating from a lower-right fault segment toward the upper-left region where the mainshock began, alongside a precursory decrease in the b-value. This is a paper-level laboratory seismology result.
organization: Institute of Geophysics, China Earthquake Administration; MIT; University of Strasbourg/CNRS

evidence.tested: In biaxial stick-slip experiments on a 0.85 m saw-cut granodiorite fault, the AEbagging ensemble deep-learning picker generated acoustic-emission catalogs for eight laboratory earthquake cycles.
evidence.unknown: This is an interpretation of eight controlled stick-slip events on one laboratory fault, not evidence that the same migration pattern is a reliable precursor to natural earthquakes. The authors suggest a possible relation to fault-surface roughness; that causal explanation is not established. The result depends on the model-generated event catalog.
evidence.ai_role: A supervised ensemble of deep neural networks detected acoustic emissions and picked their primary arrivals from continuous multichannel laboratory recordings; its generated event catalogs enabled the authors to resolve the temporal and spatial foreshock migration pattern during nucleation.
